headline: Coastal Access and Shuttle Reservation Check
reservation: The park does not charge a general entrance fee. Use official coastal bus services to reach sections of the trail without using a car; check the Pembrokeshire Coast website for seasonal shuttle timetables and wheelchair-accessible beach services which may require a book-and-collect arrangement.

days.title: Mountains to Estuaries

stops.name: Pentre Ifan
stops.detail: Visit this internationally significant prehistoric site located in the northern inland section.

stops.name: Preseli Hills
stops.detail: Hike the wild moorlands that offer a mountainous contrast to the park's coastal cliffs.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local coastal roads; conditions vary
days.note: Paths in the Preseli Hills involve varied terrain compared to the managed coastal trail.

days.title: Wildlife and Islands

stops.name: St Davids Head
stops.detail: Explore one of the most spectacular stretches of coastal scenery recommended since the park's founding.

stops.name: Oriel y Parc
stops.detail: Stop at the National Park Discovery Centre to view exhibitions and gather seasonal nature info.

days.note: Island excursions to Skomer or Ramsey are weather-dependent and require local transfer.

days.title: Castles and Stacks

stops.name: Elegug Stacks
stops.detail: Observe razorbills and guillemots nesting on these detached limestone pillars during spring.

stops.name: Carew Castle
stops.detail: Visit this historic site to learn about the cultural heritage of the southern Pembrokeshire coast.

days.note: Access to military training areas like Castlemartin may be restricted; check official notices.

intel.title: Trailhead Parking
intel.text: Parking is available near major beaches like Marloes and Broad Haven. Use official park lots to avoid blocking narrow access lanes for local residents and farmers.

intel.title: Rural Connectivity
intel.text: Mobile reception is intermittent along the cliff-top sections of the Pembrokeshire Coast Path. Download maps before setting off on long sections where GPS and data may fail.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Main fuel and supply hubs are located in Pembroke Dock, Haverfordwest, and Tenby. Coastal villages may have limited services for larger vehicles.

intel.title: Walking Pacing
intel.text: The path involves 35,000 feet of total ascent; allow significantly more time than a flat walk. Use seasonal coastal buses to return to your vehicle after one-way walks.

intel.title: Accessible Coastline
intel.text: Seventeen locations now support a beach wheelchair book-and-collect service. Several stretches of the path are accessible to wheelchair users and families with prams.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental vehicles at major transport hubs, then head to St Davids or Tenby for supplies and visitor orientation.
plan.vehicle: Cars are ideal for coastal lanes; RVs should check width restrictions on minor roads leading to remote beaches.
plan.goldenHour: Strumble Head is a named location for sunset spotting, though visibility depends on coastal mist.
